model: NAV plus exit discount: 5-year NAV total-return build capitalised at cost of equity (closed-end investment trust, NAV route; not an owner-FCF DCF)

inputs.nav_asof: 2026-10-08 (daily NAV RNS 'Net Asset Value(s)' published 9 Oct 2026; cum income)
inputs.nav_basis_note: Primary anchor is NAV with borrowings at fair value (the Company's headline KPI and the basis of its published discount). The loan notes (GBP987m book, coupons 1.65-3.65%, maturities 2036-2062) are worth less than par at current rates, so NAV-at-fair exceeds NAV-at-par by ~38p. Using par instead would lower every intrinsic value by ~2.2%.
inputs.share_count_basis: Total Voting Rights RNS 1 Oct 2026: 1,484,780,880 issued less 438,589,022 in treasury = 1,046,191,858. Treasury rose from 381.9m (post 24.75m issuance to 21 May 2026 at a premium) to 438.6m, i.e. ~56.7m shares (~GBP850m) bought back June-Sept 2026 as the discount re-opened. Held flat in the model: the valuation is per share of NAV; buyback accretion (~0.4%/yr at an 8% discount) is inside the base total-return assumption, not a share-count path.
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-03-31 (debt, cash); NAV and shares per the October 2026 RNS above
inputs.total_debt_note: 31 Mar 2026 book: bank loans 568.7 + 2026 debenture 50.1 (repaid) + irredeemable debenture 0.7 + loan notes 986.6 = GBP1,606.2m. Gearing 11% at FY2026, 8% at 30 Jun 2026. Debt is inside NAV already; it is NOT deducted again anywhere in this model.
inputs.net_debt_note: Shown for audit only. A trust's borrowings are already netted in NAV per share; subtracting them again would double-count (SKILL.md non-FCF trap #1).
inputs.private_companies_asof: 2026-06-30 (51 holdings; 41.5% of total assets at 31 Mar 2026 before SpaceX's June 2026 IPO reclassified the largest position as listed)
inputs.largest_holding: SpaceX 25.6% of portfolio at 30 Jun 2026 (listed 12 Jun 2026 at US$135; post-IPO lock-up)
inputs.fcf_note: Not an FCF model. FY2026 reported operating cash flow (-GBP68.7m) is negative because a trust's investment purchases sit in operating activities; it carries no information about value. last_fcf is deliberately null.
inputs.sbc_source: not applicable - the trust has no employees; Baillie Gifford's ad valorem fee (0.33% OCR, no performance fee) is the cost and is already inside NAV total return
inputs.buyback_cash_note: FY2026 (year to 31 Mar 2026). FY2025: GBP1,747.6m. Board policy: buy back at a discount, issue at a premium (24.75m shares issued Apr-May 2026).
inputs.price_note: scottishmortgage.com showed 1673p 'as at 9 Oct 15:30' but Yahoo's 9 Oct bar high was 1648p and the 52-week high is 1651.5p, so the website figure is a feed artefact; the Yahoo close is used. Not after-hours; not volatile.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in GBP; LSE quote in pence (GBp, 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 = GBp per GBP (model -> quote). All per-share figures in this file (NAV, dividends, intrinsic values, entry prices) are in pence so they compare directly with current_price; money inputs are GBP millions. No currency risk between statements and quote; the underlying portfolio is ~60% USD-denominated, which is a NAV risk, not an fx-bridge issue.
inputs.units: GBP millions; per-share figures in pence
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 10.0% in GBP: 10-year gilt ~4.5% + beta ~1.1 x 5% equity risk premium. Applied to the trust's shares, not a WACC - the flows (NAV growth and dividends) are already post-interest and post-fee. The same 10% is used in all three scenarios so that the scenarios differ only in the NAV path and exit discount.
inputs.notes: MODEL: NAV/NTA plus exit discount (SKILL.md routing row 'LIC, investment trust, closed-end fund'). Scottish Mortgage is a closed-end investment trust: its value is the portfolio it owns, marked daily, less borrowings. An owner-FCF DCF would discount a negative operating cash flow that contains investment purchases; EBITDA, revenue and EPS are fair-value noise. The model compounds today's NAV-at-fair per share at a scenario NAV total return for five years (less dividends paid out), applies a scenario exit discount to the year-5 NAV, and discounts the exit value plus dividends at a 10% cost of equity. Entry prices use the same cashflows at the 15% hurdle. House and street bases coincide (no SBC), so band_position is null. Built by hand (not the owner-FCF Drivers/dcf_engine route), matching the BIT.NZ and MLN.NZ trust precedents; the dashboard slider engine cannot re-derive a NAV model from component fields and will fall back to the recorded values.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case NAV total return assumption (long-run global equity return ~8% + ~0.5% net gearing contribution + ~0.4% buyback accretion at an 8% discount - 0.33% ongoing charges, no manager alpha assumed); bracketed by the 10-year NAV TR of 18.3% p.a. and the 5-year NAV TR of 2.4% p.a.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders' funds shrank 4.0% p.a. over five years while NAV per share rose 1.4% p.a. and NAV total return was 2.4% p.a.: the gap is GBP5.3bn of buybacks (shares 1,421.6m -> 1,078.2m FY2021-FY2026, 1,046.2m at 1 Oct 2026). Equity CAGR is therefore not a growth proxy for a trust; NAV per share and NAV total return are the right series. Revenue (portfolio income), EPS and FCF CAGRs are meaningless for a capital-growth trust whose P&L is dominated by fair-value movements and whose operating cash flow includes investment purchases.

discount_history_pct_debt_at_fair.pre_2022: traded at a premium (shares issued every year FY2017-FY2022)

scenario_narratives.base: NAV total return 9% p.a. for five years: the FTSE All-World's long-run ~8% plus ~0.5% from 8% net gearing at a 3.6% cost of debt and ~0.4% buyback accretion, less 0.33% ongoing charges, with no manager alpha assumed - the 10-year record (18.3% p.a.) and the 5-year record (2.4% p.a., including a 50%+ drawdown) bracket it widely. Exit discount 8%: the FY2025-26 year-end discounts were 9.0% and 9.5%, the AIC Global sector averaged 5-10%, the Board buys back at any discount and issued at a premium in April-May 2026, and the trust traded at a premium for the five years to 2022. At a 10% cost of equity the fair value is ~4-5% below today's price: today's 7.9% discount is roughly the right discount for a geared, concentrated growth portfolio, not a bargain.
scenario_narratives.bull: NAV total return 15% p.a.: the AI-infrastructure and SpaceX/Starlink theses compound as the managers expect (10-year NAV TR was 18.3% p.a.), the post-IPO SpaceX position, Anthropic, ByteDance and Stripe realise or re-rate upward, and the shares return to the premium they carried in 2017-2021 (exit discount 0%) so the Board issues rather than buys back. Fair value ~35% above today's price.
scenario_narratives.bear: NAV flat for five years (0% total return): SpaceX de-rates after the lock-up expires and private marks (20% of the portfolio, 51 companies, five of which are three-quarters of the exposure) are cut, with a rate-driven growth sell-off of the 2022 kind inside the window, so the five-year return repeats the FY2021-26 experience of ~2% p.a. or worse. The discount widens to 15% (FY2026's low was -15.9%; 2022-23 saw ~-20%) despite buybacks. Fair value ~42% below today's price. Gearing (8%, covenant cap 35%) adds volatility, not solvency risk.

base.years_note: Twelve-month steps from the 8 Oct 2026 NAV anchor (Y5 ~ Oct 2031), not fiscal years

bull.years_note: Twelve-month steps from the 8 Oct 2026 NAV anchor (Y5 ~ Oct 2031), not fiscal years

bear.years_note: Twelve-month steps from the 8 Oct 2026 NAV anchor (Y5 ~ Oct 2031), not fiscal years

base.implied_exit_multiple: n/a - trust valued on P/NAV (year-5 NAV x (1 - exit discount)), not an earnings multiple

bull.implied_exit_multiple: n/a - trust valued on P/NAV (year-5 NAV x (1 - exit discount)), not an earnings multiple

bear.implied_exit_multiple: n/a - trust valued on P/NAV (year-5 NAV x (1 - exit discount)), not an earnings multiple

entry_price.methodology: Price today at which five years of base-case dividends plus the year-5 exit value (year-5 NAV x (1 - exit discount)) discounted at the 15% hurdle equals that price. The exit value is the same NAV-based figure at every discount rate (it is not a Gordon terminal value built at the cost of equity), so the 15% row of the required-return table equals the base entry price and the 10% row equals base intrinsic value.

required_return_table.note: Each row re-discounts the same base-case dividends and year-5 NAV x (1 - 8%) exit value at that row's rate; the 10% row ties to valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row to entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.methodology: Intrinsic value (pence per share) at a 10% cost of equity, base dividend path; the centre cell (-8%, 9%) is the base case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25, the investment-trust default used for BIT.NZ and MLN.NZ, not the 15/50/35 operating-company split (which is calibrated to solvency and refinancing risk). The bear is not overweighted: gearing is 8% against a 35% covenant and the loan notes run to 2036-2062, so the downside is a market/discount outcome, not a going-concern one. The bull is not overweighted because SpaceX at a quarter of the portfolio makes the distribution of outcomes fat-tailed in both directions.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street bases coincide (no SBC in an investment trust); the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A closed-end trust is worth the discounted value of what its shares will fetch - the future NAV per share at the discount or premium the market then applies - plus the small dividend. Three things decide that: what the portfolio compounds at (dominated by SpaceX, TSMC, NVIDIA, ByteDance and ~50 private companies), where the discount settles (the Board defends it with buybacks and issues at premiums), and what return the holder requires for a geared, concentrated growth portfolio. The valuation does not forecast the holdings; it asks what an 8%-discounted, 8%-geared growth trust is worth to someone requiring 10%.
key_risks_to_valuation: SpaceX concentration (25.6% of the portfolio): a 30% move in SpaceX is ~8% of NAV before gearing; lock-up expiry after the June 2026 IPO could add supply
Private-company marks (20.4% of the portfolio, 51 holdings): valued by the manager/board; the model takes them at book in base and bull and only implicitly haircuts them in the bear path
Discount risk: the exit discount drives ~8% of base value per 8 points; the 2022-23 range reached ~-20%
Rate sensitivity: long-duration growth equities and an 8%-geared balance sheet both lose from higher real rates (FY2021-26 NAV TR was 2.4% p.a.)
Currency: ~60% of holdings are USD; a 10% GBP rally costs ~6% of NAV
NAV basis: the debt-at-fair-value anchor is ~2.2% above debt-at-par; loan-note fair value rises as gilt yields fall

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1015.7-1651.5p; prior close 1590p
data_sources.nav: RNS 'Net Asset Value(s)' 9 Oct 2026 (NAV as at 8 Oct 2026) via Investegate; cum par and cum fair both recorded
data_sources.shares: RNS 'Total Voting Rights' 1 Oct 2026 via Investegate
data_sources.financials: SMT.L_Annual_FY2026.txt (balance sheet, loan-note schedule, ten-year record, discount range, buybacks/treasury), SMT.L_Presentation_Q3-2026.txt (Q2 2026 data pack: 30 Jun 2026 NAV 1613p, discount -8.8%, gearing 8%, private 20.4%, SpaceX 25.6%, top-10 58.3%), SMT.L_Metrics.csv / kpis (NAVPerShare history)

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
